name: libmysofa
desc: Reader for AES SOFA files to get better HRTFs
why: Reads SOFA head-related transfer function files, a real door into binaural spatial audio and how ears localise sound.

brief.what_it_is: libmysofa is a small C library for reading AES SOFA files that contain head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) in the AES69-2015 standard. It takes a .sofa file (or a buffer already in memory) and a target sample rate, then gives you the HRTF filter for any requested [x,y,z] position as left and right impulse responses plus left and right delays in samples or seconds. Filters can be linearly interpolated from nearest neighbours or taken exactly as stored. The README also documents spherical-to-Cartesian coordinate helpers. The brew formula lists an executable called mysofa2json, but the README does not describe it.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a simple reader so that software can use HRTF data stored in AES SOFA files, which the author's MySofa work relies on for personal HRTF design and better binaural audio.
brief.how_it_works: mysofa_open (or the normalising, advanced, in-memory or cached variants) parses the SOFA HDF5 data and builds a nearest-neighbour search structure over the measurement grid, with optional normalisation. mysofa_getfilter_float or mysofa_getfilter_short then returns a weighted sum of the nearest neighbours' filters for a position, or the exact stored filter via the _nointerp variant. The caller applies the returned delays and convolves audio with the impulse responses using FIR filtering.

brief.install_notes: Build needs CMake, a C compiler, zlib development headers and CUnit for tests; the README's apt line also includes nodejs and git. Tests run with ctest. Installing to a system path usually needs sudo, and a non-system prefix is set with CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX. Consuming CMake projects use find_package(mysofa CONFIG) and link mysofa::mysofa-shared or mysofa::mysofa-static, and may need CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH or mysofa_DIR to find the library. The README gives no account or hardware requirements, and the brew route is not covered beyond the formula name.
brief.standout: Rather than just parsing the file, it gives a ready-made lookup: you ask for a direction and distance, and it returns the filter and interpolated delays, with a cached open that shares one copy of a HRTF in memory across handles. The README also covers big-endian testing through QEMU, which is unusual for a small audio library.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README has CI badges (AppVeyor, Coverity, codecov), a Repology packaging badge and a PayPal donation button, but shows no release version, date, or last-commit information. Its OS notes still cite Ubuntu 14.04 and OSX 7.3 CI, and the references date from 2017, so recent activity cannot be confirmed from the README alone.
brief.caveats: The README targets C and builds with CMake; it documents Linux, OSX and Windows (Windows through Visual Studio 2015 CI and MinGW via FFmpeg). Big-endian support was checked only through emulation. Interpolated lookups can skip true nearest neighbours if the search step is set too coarse, so the step must match the SOFA file's grid. The README does not describe mysofa2json, so its usage is unknown from these sources. The README does not state a licence; the disclaimer says the remaining source is BSD-3-Clause, while the K-D tree and resampler come from other authors. No brew caveats were given.
quotes: This is a simple set of C functions to read AES SOFA files, if they contain HRTFs stored according to the AES69-2015 standard
Libmysofa compiles for Linux operating systems, OSX and Windows.
The greater the neighbor_*_step, the faster the neighbors search. The algorithm will end up skipping true nearest neighbors if these values are set too high.
